python3 tools/mem.py ask "B3 packet design; five points the build rests on. (1) checks/stage_B3.py holds every packet file to 50 KB, so B3 cannot reuse B2's self-contained packets of up to 180 KB. Proposal: whole-room batches packed to 40 items and about 44 KB of rendered text, so most batches are one file; a room larger than that is a batch by itself, served in parts to one reader (MANIFEST group and part, as packets.py B3 writes them). 83 rooms render over 50 KB; the largest is ainbowroad, 268 KB. (2) leagueoflegends t02 renders 89 KB alone; no part holds it under 50 KB. Serve it as one file over the ceiling (the check refuses it), or split its concepts across two consecutive parts of the same reader, one item and one line? (3) Gold: the stage seeds gold items into live batches as extra copies, but check_batches refuses an item whose room is not among the batch's rooms, and the check leg counts every returned line against n_items. Proposal: list each gold copy in items and in gold_items, so n_items counts every position the reader answers, and the handler exempts listed gold copies from the whole-room rule. (4) The check counts every non-prediction line of a return against n_items, while packets.py's MANIFEST count excludes lines carrying primary or revises. Proposal: the multiplacement records ride on the item line as a multiplacement_log list (as in B2), and the second pass is written as lines carrying revises after the pass-1 lines; how should fleet.py store pass 2 so the check reads it apart? (5) The warm-up stays in reserve: B2 showed agreement within packets falling, not rising, though notes-B2.md had declared a 10-item warm-up. The exemplar arm is not served, as in B2." --assume "I build on the proposals: (1) as above; (2) leagueoflegends t02 split across two consecutive parts of one reader, one item and one line, the split named in notes-B3.md; (3) gold copies in items and gold_items; (4) records on the line, pass-2 lines carrying revises; (5) warm-up in r
